html:
The Hamzanama is a huge illustrated book of adventure stories made for the Mughal emperor Akbar from about 1562 to 1577. It was the first great project of Mughal painting.

The stories follow Amir Hamza, an uncle of the Prophet Muhammad, through a fantasy world of giants, demons, spies and battles. The tales were told aloud at court, and Akbar, who could not read, loved them.

The scale was enormous. About 1,400 large paintings on cotton cloth filled 14 volumes, each picture with its text on the back. The work took some fifteen years. It was led by two Persian masters, Mir Sayyid Ali and Abd al-Samad, who had come to India with Akbar's father, a move shown on the chart as Persian painters join Humayun. Under them worked dozens of Indian painters.

The result mixed Persian fine line with Indian colour, movement and close looking at nature. That mix became the Mughal style. Fewer than 200 paintings survive, scattered among museums such as the MAK in Vienna and the Victoria and Albert Museum in London.
sum: The Hamzanama is a huge illustrated book of adventure stories made for the Mughal emperor Akbar from about 1562 to 1577. It was the first great project of Mughal painting.
